title: Continuous Medical Oxygen Rationing
real_world_story: A field hospital operating during a respiratory illness surge has an emergency bulk supply of C liters of liquid medical oxygen. N hospital wards have requested oxygen allocations. Ward i requires up to w_i liters of oxygen and will achieve an aggregate clinical efficacy score of v_i if its full request is granted. Liquid oxygen is a continuous fluid: delivering a fraction f (0 <= f <= 1) of ward i's request delivers f * v_i in clinical efficacy. The emergency coordinator must determine the maximum total clinical efficacy achievable from the available C liters.
problem_statement: Given total capacity C and N items, each with maximum volume w_i and full efficacy value v_i, calculate the maximum clinical efficacy achievable by taking arbitrary fractions f_i (0 <= f_i <= 1) of items such that the total volume does not exceed C.
task: Compute the maximum total clinical efficacy, formatted as a floating-point number with exactly two decimal places.
input_format:
The first line contains two space-separated integers N and C, the number of ward requests and the total oxygen capacity in liters.
The next N lines each contain two space-separated integers w_i and v_i, representing the volume requested and the total clinical efficacy for ward i.
output_format: Print the maximum clinical efficacy as a floating-point number rounded and formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

examples.explanation: Efficacy ratios per liter: Ward 1 = 60/10 = 6.0; Ward 2 = 100/20 = 5.0; Ward 3 = 120/30 = 4.0. Take 10 L from Ward 1 (efficacy 60.0, remaining C = 40). Take 20 L from Ward 2 (efficacy 100.0, remaining C = 20). Take 20 L from Ward 3 (fraction 20/30 * 120 = 80.0). Total efficacy = 60 + 100 + 80 = 240.00.
Ward 1 ratio is 5.0, Ward 2 ratio is 3.0. Take all 10 L of Ward 1 (50) and 5 L of Ward 2 (5/10 * 30 = 15). Total efficacy = 50 + 15 = 65.00.

real_world_takeaway: When resources are continuous and divisible, sorting by value density (value per unit volume) yields the mathematically optimal allocation with greedy efficiency.
